description: The SCEC Broadband Platform is a software system that generates broadband seismograms from 0 to more than 20 Hz for historical and scenario earthquakes in California, Eastern North America and Japan using several alternative simulation methods, including the GP, SDSU, Irikura, Song and UCSB methods. In validation mode it simulates recorded events such as Landers, Ridgecrest and Chino Hills and produces goodness-of-fit plots for pseudo-spectral acceleration and Fourier amplitude spectra against observed records; in scenario mode it runs user-defined ruptures with station lists. Release 22.4.0 of September 2022 added multi-segment ruptures, a ten times faster low-frequency module and new Green's functions for the Southern Walker Lane. It is developed and supported by the SCEC Research Computing Group (Fabio Silva, Philip Maechling and others), with the preferred reference Maechling et al. (2015) in Seismological Research Letters. The code is accessible free on GitHub and Zenodo, with Docker images for laptops; SCEC-developed parts are under the BSD 3-Clause licence and individual method codes may carry their own open licences. Caveats: full installations need Linux and high-performance computing, and region velocity models and validation events are limited to the supported regions. It supports generation of ground-motion time histories for seismic fragility and network damage simulation of bridges, pipelines, lifelines and buildings; a related record is the OpenQuake Engine.
